walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who do Sikhs consider their living guru today?
options: Sikhs follow a current living guru as their leader.
Sikhs consider the Dalai Lama their current guru.
The Guru Granth Sahib — the Sikh scripture, declared the eternal guru by Guru Gobind Singh after the line of ten human gurus ended.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Substance dualism means men and women are different.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Sikhs consider the Dalai Lama their current guru.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
